text:
name: read_aloud_slowly
does: Reads the text on the screen out loud at the speed the listener picks, and can cast the voice to a nearby speaker.
inputs: the text or page to read, how fast to read it, and a cap on how loud it may get
people say:
- My eyes are tired, can you say this page out loud?
- Slow down, I can't follow that voice.
- Read me the letter while I stir the hot soup.
- Put the story on the kitchen speaker so everyone hears it.
- Not so loud, please, and a bit slower.

Rosa runs a small flower shop and she is always tired by the evening. One night she lay in bed with the window open, because the room was hot, and she could not sleep. She was afraid she would cry from tiredness in the morning. 'Wake me up tomorrow at six,' she told her phone, 'and make the sound soft, not a loud beep.' The assistant understood that she wanted an alarm for six o'clock the next morning with a gentle ringtone. It set the alarm and said, 'Your alarm is set for tomorrow at six with a soft tone.' Rosa smiled, put the phone on the table and fell asleep a few minutes later.

Omar drives a delivery van, and at lunch he eats in the parking lot with a cup of tea from his flask. It was a slow day, so he picked up his phone and typed in a hurry: whats on at the cinma tonite near me. The assistant understood that he wanted to see the films playing at cinemas close to him that evening. It read his location and showed three cinemas with their times. One of them had a daily late show at nine thirty. Omar liked that, because he would climb into the van at six and be done by eight. He asked the assistant to save the nine thirty time, and it did.

A time zone is a part of the world where all the clocks show the same hour. When you travel, or call a friend far away, the time can be very different. A huge number of people check the clock on their phone to see what time it is in another city. The phone knows where you are and sets the time by itself, so you do not have to cough up the answer from memory. People say things like, 'What time is it in Tokyo?' or 'Is it morning for my sister in Lima?' If you move to a new place, you can say, 'Change my clock to local time.' Some people also ask for a second clock, to see home and away at once.

They want help planning what to eat for the week.
meal plan for the week
what should we eat this week
plan dinners for 5 days pls
I need ideas for lunches that will last in a bag until noon
can you plan meals for a trip, we leave on frdiay
I have no idea what to cook, can you sort out my week with less meat
Could you please help me put together a menu for the next seven days? I would like it to cost less than last week.
what's for dinner every night, I'm tired of choosing

People count days all the time. You might want to know how many days are left until a birthday, a holiday or the end of school. You might also want to know how old someone is, or how many eggs are left in the fridge. A phone can do the counting for you. You choose a start day and an end day, or you give it a thing to count. Some people hate counting by hand, and a few get angry when the number is wrong. To change the answer, people say things like, 'Count from Monday instead,' 'Leave out the weekends,' or 'Add one more day.' Then the new number appears, and you can read it out or share it with someone.

Mr. Hall does not like phones. He hates all the little buttons, and his granddaughter's screen looks pricey and confusing. But she had a test on Friday, and she was staying with him. 'Can you tell me when the spelling test is?' he asked the speaker in the hall, speaking slowly. 'Remind her tomorrow at seven to look at her words.' The assistant understood that he wanted a reminder for seven o'clock the next morning, about the spelling test. It said, 'I will remind you tomorrow at seven to study the spelling words.' Then the dryer buzzed in the next room. Mr. Hall smiled. It was easier than he had thought, and he had not pressed a single button.

Dana works in an office and was bored in a long meeting. She remembered that her email password was old, so she took out her phone and said, 'Change my email password to something new.' Then she stopped. 'No wait, not the email one. I mean the work chat password.' The assistant understood her correction. It said it would not touch the email, and it opened the settings for the work chat. It asked her to type the new password herself so that nobody else would hear it. Dana wrote it down on a paper tag that she kept on her belt, then she asked the assistant to unmute the meeting and turned back to her screen.

An alarm is a sound that wakes you up or tells you that time is up. People use alarms in the morning, and they use timers in the kitchen to know when the eggs are done. Both do one thing: they count down or wait for a time, and then they ring. Some people warn the phone to be extra loud if they sleep deeply. To change an alarm, people say, 'Make it ten minutes later,' 'Snooze for five more,' 'Turn it off for the weekend' or 'Set a timer for twenty minutes.' If you use the lock screen, you can often stop the sound there. If you do not need it anymore, you can cancel it for total quiet.

name: choose_vacuum_zone
does: Tells a robot vacuum which room or part of a room to clean, and when to open its lid or start, and it can download a new floor map when the house changes.
inputs: the room or area, the time to start, and how strong the cleaning should be
people say:
- The kitchen floor is a mess, can you clean it now?
- Send the little robot to the hallway.
- Don't do the bedroom today.
- Run the vacuum every day at noon in the living room.
- Crumbs everywhere under the table, please sort it out.

name: homework_due_alert
does: Reminds a student about a school task before it is late and lists what is still not finished.
inputs: the subject, the name of the task, and the day it is due
people say:
- When is my science project due?
- Remind me about the math sheet so I don't post it too late.
- What do I still have to hand in this week?
- Tell me an hour before the English essay is due.
- I feel like I forgot something for school, take a look.
- Don't let me miss the history quiz, I'll even take a pill for my headache first.

Ben is a gardener, and one cool morning he was painting a fence when he wanted a drink. He said to the kitchen speaker, 'Make me a coffee, but I don't want any sugar and no milk, just plain and strong.' The assistant understood that he wanted a black coffee with nothing added. It sent the order to the coffee machine and said, 'One strong black coffee, no sugar, no milk.' A minute later the machine began to zoom and hum. Ben wiped the paint off his hands, and he carried the cup to a neat bench in the yard. It tasted just right.

Lena woke up with her eyes half closed, and her phone buzzed on the pillow. It was her friend Mia, asking about breakfast. 'Reply to Mia and say I'll be there at ten,' Lena said. Then, after a yawn, 'No, I mean eleven. And call her honey, she likes that.' The assistant understood the correction. It changed the time from ten to eleven in the text. Then it read the message back: 'Hi honey, I'll be there at eleven.' Lena said, 'Send it.' She could hardly hear herself, but the assistant heard her well enough. The text was sent, and her phone was working fine. She went back to sleep for ten minutes.

bigger text
make the letters larger

Zoom in a bit, the print is tiny
make the font bigger, no wait, just for the messages, the rest is fine
The holiday photos look fine, but the words under them are so small that I feel sour about it. Could you make them bigger?
Help, I am squinting at my phone
Could you please make everything easier to read? My eyes are not as sharp as they were.

weaker coffee please
make my coffee a bit lighter
not so strong, thanks
Half the coffee this time, I'm having a polite little breakfast with my aunt
this is way too bitter, can you fix that
could you make the drink half as strong as it was yesterday

They want to know how many days are left until a date.
how many days until my birthday
days until the weekend?
how long till the holiday
It's a mild day and I think summer is far away, how many days until June?
I'm counting down to the pancake party on Sunday, what's left?
When does my vacation start, in days?
How many sleeps until Christmas, I think it is soon.
Could you tell me how many days remain before the exam?

A budget is a plan for your money. You write down how much comes in each month, and how much goes out for rent, food, bills and fun. People use a budget so that they can save a little and not run out of money before the month ends. Some months you must be careful, like in the cold season, when heating bills grow. Your phone can scan a receipt or a bill and add it to your list. To change the plan, people say, 'Give me less for snacks,' 'Put fifty into savings,' 'Show what I spent this week' or 'Move my rent date.' Then the numbers on the page change, and you can see what is left.

name: find_parking_spot
does: Looks for a free place to park near a street or building and starts a parking meter if the person wants to begin paying.
inputs: where the person is going, how long they will stay, and how far they will walk
people say:
- Where can I leave the car near the library?
- I need a spot for two hours, nothing too expensive.
- Is there any parking left by the stadium?
- Start the meter, I'm going in for a quick run to the store.
- Find me something steady and safe for the night.

Person: Put a meeting on my calendar, please.
Assistant: Sure. What day and time should it be?
Person: Tomorrow. I don't want it early, I just woke up and the room is still dim.
Assistant: Understood, not early. Would ten o'clock work?
Person: Make it eleven. It's a moment to talk with my boss.
Assistant: Okay, a meeting tomorrow at eleven. What should I write as the title?
Person: Write 'Talk with Mr. Green'.
Assistant: Done. 'Talk with Mr. Green' is on your calendar tomorrow at eleven.

Mrs. Lopez is a retired teacher, and she burned her finger on the oven in July. Her kitchen was foggy with steam, and she felt a little shaky. 'What do I do for a burn?' she asked her phone. 'Should I put butter on it?' Before it answered she said, 'No, wait, I mean cold water. My neighbor said butter is wrong.' The assistant understood the correction. It said, 'Hold the burn under cool running water for ten minutes. Do not use butter or ice.' It also offered to call for help if the burn got worse. Mrs. Lopez held her hand under the tap, and she said, 'Thank you.' The pain got a little better.

Person: Start a timer for the game.
Assistant: Sure. How long should the timer run?
Person: Twenty-five minutes. I just got home from the night shift and I want a small game with my kids before I sleep.
Assistant: Okay, a timer for twenty-five minutes. Do you want a sound at the end?
Person: Yes, a soft one. And can you tell me the score of the match last night?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't see the score of your game, because I don't know the numbers. If you tell me, I can keep them.
Person: Okay, I'll say them out loud. Clear the old score too.
Assistant: Done. The old score is cleared and the timer is running.

They want help packing warm things for a night outside.
pack list for a cold night in a tent
what should I bring, it gets chilly up there
help me pack warm for camping
It's going to be freezing by the lake, what do I need?
Should I take a black wool hat, or is that too much? What else do I need for the hills?
My sleeping bag has a cut in the wire frame and the nights are very cold, tell me what to bring
What should I wear for a night under the stars, in October?
Could you please make a list of warm things for the weekend camping trip?

close the curtains
shut the blinds pls

the sun is in my eyes

can you pull the blinds half way down, I'm watching a movie and eating noodles and dont want any glare

Assistant: I can do both. How long should do not disturb stay on?
Person: Until three o'clock. I worked all night and I'm trying to sleep. I may forget to turn it off.
Assistant: Okay. The screen is dimmer and do not disturb is on until three. Should calls from your family still come through?

Person: Fine, add it.

A workout is a plan for exercise. It might say do ten push-ups, rest for one minute, then do ten more. Each group of the same move is called a set, and each time you do the move is a rep. Rest days matter, because your body gets stronger when you stop. Do not push too hard, since a heavy weight can be dangerous if you are tired. Some people even bring a tent to the park and train outside. To change a workout, people say, 'Make it easier,' 'Add one more set,' 'Do fewer reps,' 'Stop the timer' or 'Skip today, I need a rest day.' The plan then changes to match what you said.

Writing a letter or a story usually begins with a rough draft. You put down your ideas first, and you fix the words later. A tall pile of paper is not needed any more, since a phone or computer does the checking for you. It can fix spelling, count the words and read the text back. If an email asks for you to reply by tonight, you can do it fast. To change what you wrote, people say, 'Make it shorter,' 'Use simpler words,' 'Fix my spelling,' 'Sound more polite' or 'How many words is this?' The text then changes. You can always say, 'Go back to the first version,' and your old words return.

Your phone does many things in the background, and the battery is the thing most people watch. When it gets low, the phone can turn on a mode that saves power. The screen gets dimmer, and some apps stop working. You can also schedule quiet hours, so that it does not ring at night. This is called do not disturb. If you get a call while it's on, the phone stays silent. People say, 'Turn on battery saver,' 'Make the screen darker,' 'Be quiet until morning,' or 'Free up space, I have no room for photos.' It may sound windy and complicated, but it is only a few words, like fertile soil for a small garden.

Sam just moved to the city and his flat felt cold, because the heater made a strange noise. 'My heater won't work right,' he told his phone. 'Can you find someone to fix it? Half of the radiators are cold, and the other half make a loud noise. I want a repair man who comes this week and doesn't cost more than fifty dollars.' The assistant understood that he needed a repair visit for a broken heater. It looked for repair shops near him and found one that charged less than fifty. It called the number, and the phone began to ring. Sam made himself a cup of bitter coffee, and a juice for dinner, and waited for an answer.

Kim woke up late and her head was still full of sleep. She picked up her phone and typed fast: set a focus timer for 25 minuts and keep the phne silent. The assistant understood her message even with the typos. It started a focus timer for twenty-five minutes and put the phone on silent mode. It said, 'Focus timer started. Notifications are off.' Kim put her toy robot on the shelf, tapped the screen to adjust the brightness, and sat down at the desk to work. When the timer ended, the phone gave a gentle chime, and she took a short break.

First aid means the small things you do to help someone who is hurt, before a doctor can see them. For a cut, you clean it and cover it. For a small burn, you hold it under cool water. If something gets in your eye, you rinse it with water and do not rub. People ask a phone what to do when they cannot sell the problem to anyone nearby, and the phone gives steps. They say things like, 'What do I do for a burn?', 'Call for help,' 'Say the steps again slowly,' or 'Is this bad enough for a doctor?' If someone is badly hurt, go away from danger and call the emergency number right away.

Ana is a nurse, and she came home at seven in the morning, very tired after a night shift. She had to write a short note for her manager, but she did not have the speed to type it. 'Write a message to my manager,' she told her phone. 'Say that I can carry the Friday shift, but I need Saturday off. And send it tomorrow at nine, not now.' The assistant understood that she wanted a short email scheduled for the next morning. It wrote the message and read it back. It checked the spelling and said, 'Your email is ready to send tomorrow at nine.' Ana nodded and went to bed.

Jo had just finished a night shift at the hospital and her eyes hurt. At home she typed on her phone, in a hurry: print my pass ticket, the wide one, and chek the ink. The assistant understood that she wanted to print a ticket and see how much ink was left. It sent the file to the printer in the hall. Then it told her, 'The black ink is low, about ten percent.' Jo said, 'Can you spell out the name of the right ink for me?' The assistant read the label name slowly, letter by letter. A dollar was all she had in her pocket, so she added ink to her shopping list instead.

A phone call is the simplest way to talk with someone who is far away. You tap a name or say it, and the phone rings the other person. If nobody picks up, you can leave a voicemail. If you miss a call, the phone shows who it was, so you can call back. People often add a friend to the list of favorites, so that a nearby tap is all it takes. Speakerphone lets many people hear the call together, like when you share an album of photos. To change a call, people say, 'Put it on speaker,' 'Turn the volume up,' 'Call him back' or 'Mute me for a second.' Then the phone does just that.

stop the beeping
turn off the alarm
it's only toast, cancel the alarm
the white thing on the ceiling keeps screaming, shut it up

Greg works in an office and his day is always busy. On Monday he had a big meeting at nine, and he was afraid he would be late. At his desk he said to the speaker, 'Set an alarm for tomorrow at seven, and call it Meeting.' The assistant understood that he wanted a morning alarm with a name. It also noticed a timer already running, one that Greg had set for his lunch. It said, 'Your seven o'clock alarm called Meeting is set. The timer for lunch is still on.' Greg zipped up his bag, and went home. The next day the alarm rang right on time.

Tom was in a hurry, because his dad was waiting in the car, and he had a sick feeling that he forgot his homework. He grabbed his phone and said, 'Open my math homework. How many problems are due today?' The assistant understood that he wanted the math assignment and the number of problems. It opened the file and said, 'Your math sheet has twenty-five problems and is due today at noon.' Tom said, 'Read me the first five.' The assistant read them out in a clear voice. Tom did the first one in his head, then ran to the car with the phone still in his hand.

Assistant: I can help with that. Which pizza would you like, and what address should I send it to?
Person: the usual, with chese. send it to the garage on Pine street
Assistant: Okay, a cheese pizza to the garage on Pine Street. How much height of tip should I add? Ten percent?

Person: no keep it
Assistant: Done. The order is placed, and it should arrive in about thirty minutes.

An estimate is a guess about what something will cost. People make one before they spend money. For example, you may estimate that groceries for a week cost about eighty dollars. A good guess keeps your mouth from watering over something you cannot afford. When you plan a budget, you write the guess next to the real number and see which is more. If you spend less than planned, the extra money goes to savings. People say, 'Estimate my bills for next month,' 'Show me what I spent on food,' 'Lower the food limit,' or 'Give me less to spend on games.' The page then shows the new total.

They want the phone to start showing alerts again after a break.
turn notifications back on
resume my alerts
start the pings again
I want to see likes again, no, only comments
my battery is low, but I still want to know when my sister posts
Can you switch the likes alert back on? Actually only for my own photos, not for the meter app I follow.
I paused everything last week, please let it all come back now
Could you turn my social alerts back on for the weekend? I missed a few messages and I felt bad about it.

A meal plan is a list of what you will eat on each day. People write one so they do not have to think about dinner every evening. It also helps you buy only what you need. On Monday you might roast a chicken, and on Tuesday you use what is left in a soup. It is smart to plan simple meals for busy days. If you want to dive into the depth of it, you can add lunches and snacks. To change the plan, people say, 'No fish this week,' 'Make it cheaper,' 'Swap Tuesday and Thursday,' 'Add a vegetable dish' or 'Something light on Friday.' Then you get a new list.

Person: Read me my new email.
Assistant: You have one unread email, from Mr. Park. Do you want me to read all of it?
Person: Just the top part. I'm driving, I don't want to miss my turn.
Assistant: He says, the meeting is moved to Thursday. Do you want to reply?
Person: Yes. Write a short note saying I'll be there, and add twenty-five minutes to the time.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't change his meeting time, but I can tell him you may be late. Should I write that?
Person: Yes, send it. That old blue logo looks ugly, by the way.
Assistant: Your note is sent.

Hank is a gardener, and his small field was a few centimeters from a flood after the rain. He wanted a break at the seaside. 'Book a room for two nights from Friday,' he told the phone. 'Wait, I mean three nights. And I want a soft bed, not a hard one.' The assistant understood the change from two nights to three. It looked for rooms near the beach and picked one with a soft bed. 'A room for three nights from Friday is ready to book,' it said. 'Do you want to miss breakfast, or add it?' Hank laughed, and said to add it.

Priya was late, and when she got into her car it was freezing. 'Brr, it's so cold in here,' she said to the dashboard. The car heard her. It understood that she wanted the heat on, so it turned the warm air on and said so. Then she added, 'And I have an invitation for lunch, so I need to know if I have enough fuel.' The assistant said the tank was half full, enough for the drive. The light on the screen was bright, so she asked it to dim the display. It did. Priya pulled out of the driveway and made it to lunch in good time.

They want a meeting moved to a new time and the phone silenced.
move my meeting and mute the phone
shift the 3pm to 4pm and silence my notifications
Push back my top meeting by an hour and mute me during it
meeting later, phone quiet
I need the carrot talk with Anna to start at noon instead, and keep my phone quiet until then
Could you move my appointment to Friday morning, and also mute my alerts while I'm at the dentist?
reschedule the call to tomorrow and silence everything till then

Fred is a gardener, and he works far from the house, near the old station road. His phone showed only one bar of wifi, and the page for ship tracking kept freezing. 'Why is the internet so slow in the garden?' he asked. 'Can you make the signal twice as strong?' The assistant understood that he wanted a faster connection outside. It could not make the signal stronger itself, but it checked the router and said, 'The router is far away. Move it closer, or use the extender.' It also found that the wifi in the shallow end of the yard was weaker than in the house. Fred put the extender by the window and the page loaded.

Person: How do I get to the museum?
Assistant: Happy to help. Where are you starting from, and do you want to walk, take the bus or drive?
Person: I'm at the train station. I'm new here, so the bus please.
Assistant: Take bus 12 from stop B. The ride is about fifteen minutes. When do you want to go?
Person: Tomorrow at seven in the evening. Will it be crowded? I want to peel off my coat and sit.
Assistant: I can't tell how crowded it will be. But the next bus after seven is quieter, and the stop is one meter from the door.
Person: Good, remind me tomorrow at six thirty.

Person: 14 and 27
Assistant: Fourteen plus twenty-seven is forty-one.
Person: now times 3
Assistant: Forty-one times three is one hundred twenty-three.

Assistant: It is a square that is one centimeter on each side.

Finding a film to watch is easy when your phone helps. You say a few words, like the name of the film, and it shows where it plays and when. If you want a certain seat, you can place an order for tickets. The best seats are usually in the middle, and they sell out first. A good cinema also shows a trailer so you can see what the film is like. People change their plans often, and they say, 'Show me something funny,' 'Only films after eight,' 'Book two seats in the middle' or 'Find a cheaper show.' If many friends want to come, you can multiply the seats, for example by asking for six instead of two.

Person: Good morning. I'm very sorry to ask so early, but my grandson is coming after school and I will be out, so could you unlock the front door for him at four?
Assistant: Of course. Do you want it to stay unlocked, or lock again after he comes in?
Person: Please lock it again after about ten minutes.
Assistant: Okay. The front door will unlock at four and lock at ten past. Do you also want to give him a code?
Person: Yes. Also, can you sell my old key to the shop on the corner?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't sell things. I can tell you which shop is closest. Would you like to see the most recent visits at your door too?
Person: That would be nice, thank you.

Mrs. Reed is a retired teacher who loves to bake bread on Sunday. She had a pot of tea and an apron on, and she said to her kitchen speaker, 'Could you please help me? I am afraid I will forget the dough, because my grandchildren are coming and I will be talking all morning. Would you remind me every hour to check if the dough has risen?' The assistant understood that she wanted an hourly reminder while the dough rose. It said, 'Of course. I will remind you every hour to check the dough.' It also found a leaf of her recipe, search by search, and read her the baking time. Mrs. Reed smiled and began to knead.
